Key Nagoya Areas and Corridors
Where Nagoya Audiences Gather

Nagoya’s audiences cluster in a handful of districts and travel corridors. The right mix depends on the objective, the dates and the screens available through participating media partners. Nagoya’s extensive road network also creates opportunities to reach audiences through roadside advertising along major traffic arteries.
Meieki (Nagoya Station District)

The city’s main gateway and business district, where the Tokaido Shinkansen, JR, Meitetsu, Kintetsu and subway lines meet. Nagoya Station is described as the world’s largest station by floor area, and the surrounding towers mix offices, hotels and department stores.
Sakae
Nagoya’s central shopping, dining and entertainment district, around Hisaya-odori Park and the Nagoya TV Tower. Suited to retail, fashion, beauty and food brands.
Fushimi and Marunouchi
Office and financial districts between Meieki and Sakae, reaching professional and weekday audiences.
Kanayama and Osu
Kanayama is a major rail interchange between central Nagoya and Centrair; Osu is a busy shopping street popular with younger audiences and visitors.
Chubu Centrair International Airport
The region’s international and domestic gateway, with 11.0 million passengers in fiscal 2024, reaching business travellers, inbound visitors and outbound residents.
Aichi’s Industrial and Suburban Corridors

The roads and rail lines linking Nagoya with Toyota City, Kariya, Okazaki and other manufacturing centres, where the Toyota group and its suppliers are based. Useful for B2B, recruitment, automotive and suburban retail campaigns.
